verified_claims.claim: The Python quality gate uses paired same-case behavior deltas, a default 1.0 percentage-point effect floor, z=1.645, and activates the paired significance check at n>=5.

Regression checks use ordinary 95% Wilson intervals and adaptively resample an inconclusive raw drop until interval separation or the per-case attempt cap; the inspected path contains no anytime-valid replacement for those repeated looks.
verified_claims.scope: This does not say one pre-specified Wilson interval is invalid; the certification claim is only that repeated adaptive inspection is not made anytime-valid by this code.

verified_claims.scope: Establishes that the auto holdout is not a permanently untouched terminal outer lockbox; it does not establish empirical overfitting.

material_scope_correction.title: Nonuniform case weights enter the significance bound despite the source docstring saying they do not
source_mechanism: gate.py constructs case_weights from every train case with weight != 1.0 and passes aligned weights to assess_quality_gain.
scoregain.py states that weights scale effect size only and 'never touch the significance test'.
But assess_quality_gain sets mean_delta to the weighted mean when weights are present, then uses that same mean_delta as the center of mean_delta - 1.645 * (sample_stddev(raw_deltas)/sqrt(n)).
The standard error remains computed from unweighted raw deltas. Thus the resulting lower bound is a hybrid: its center is weighted while its standard error is unweighted.

mechanical_counterexample.interpretation: Both 2.0pp unweighted and 8.75pp weighted means clear the 1.0pp effect floor, but only the weighted-center code path clears the significance check. Therefore nonuniform weights can flip the significance verdict even though the docstring says weights do not touch significance.

material_scope_correction.scope_revision: The checkpoint phrase 'one-sided 95% lower confidence bound on the mean paired delta' is accurate for uniform/no-weight cases. With nonuniform configured case weights, the inspected Python implementation does not compute a standard 95% lower confidence bound for either the unweighted mean or a properly weighted mean; treat it as an implementation-specific hybrid heuristic unless separately justified.
material_scope_correction.impact_boundary: No claim is made here about Node parity, empirical failure frequency, or end-to-end acceptance rates. Other lexicographic gates can still reject a candidate before/after this quality check.
